title: Local repair, route geometry and branch identity remain separate
claim: BR-030 Terra/high passed the local coronary repair, trace and mesh checks but failed CPR distance-axis consistency. In BR-041, Astra/xhigh covered the full scored RCA-to-PDA reference within 1 mm yet failed the frozen distance and endpoint gates; Terra/high and Sol/xhigh also failed their original frozen scores. BR-042’s completed resumed Astra/xhigh artifact reached 94.0% geometry and 79.3% correctly labeled coronary length coverage at 1 mm, while both category-based pass gates remained unmet. D2/OM1 discovery or acceptance and dependent numbering remain distinct from the pending PDA-versus-inferior-RV identity review.
limitations: BR-030 supplied a damaged mask and targeted route context; its local connection success does not establish repair of the full parent tree. The separate TopCoW 244-voxel addition dispute remains clinically unadjudicated.
BR-041 and BR-042 supplied source CTA without the private scored centerlines. BR-041 distal extent review is separate from BR-042 branch identity; no score is changed by either interpretation.
BR-042’s final artifact is a resumed continuation after transport interruption, not another independent blind attempt; setup failures and timed-out partial artifacts are not completed model failures.

BR-042 geometry and original scores are retained while the mapping of reference right-3 and the PDA fork is under review. Broader noncoronary inventory lacks full reference coverage, and unmatched geometry is not automatically false anatomy.

The retained BR-042 filter replay explains a specific saved pipeline; reference-assisted diagnostics are not solver inputs or new blind-trial evidence. Selected public cases and unequal model/effort conditions establish neither population performance nor a causal benefit of extra time.
